ATLANTA, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Norfolk Southern Corporation (

) today launched a celebration of 200 years of railroading, tracing its heritage back to its first predecessor, founded in 1827. The railroad gathered employees in Birmingham, Ala. for a kickoff celebration that unveiled the first of three commemorative bicentennial locomotives, showcased employee stories and teased an upcoming Norfolk Southern Heritage Days tour.

Reaching 200 years places Norfolk Southern among a rare group of U.S. companies with roots stretching back to the beginnings of America's industrial economy. From the earliest tracks to today's modern freight network, railroading has grown and evolved alongside the nation, connecting communities, supporting businesses, and powering the nation's growth.
"For 200 years, railroads have been part of the backbone of America, connecting businesses and markets, strengthening our supply chain and helping drive the nation's economy forward,"
said Norfolk Southern President and CEO Mark George

. "None of that happens without the generations of railroaders who built this industry and the people carrying that legacy forward. As we honor our past, we're equally focused on what we are delivering today and how we're building a stronger railroad for the future of our communities, customers, and employees."
Celebrating Norfolk Southern's heritage with new campaign, NS 200 Locomotive series and community events
Norfolk Southern introduced the
GeneratioNS

campaign during an employee kickoff celebration today at its Norris Yard in Birmingham, Ala., a key hub in the railroad's operations with a proud railroading legacy. The event featured remarks from company leadership and stories from multigenerational railroaders. Locomotive No. 4980, The 1827, was unveiled; it's the first of three specially designed locomotives commemorating the anniversary, called the NS 200 Locomotive series. The locomotives will serve as moving tributes to the railroad's history, and progress that have shaped Norfolk Southern.
Beginning in Spring 2027, Norfolk Southern will celebrate with employees and communities across its network through the
Norfolk Southern Heritage Days tour

. The series of events will give employees, customers, and the public opportunities to explore the railroad's history and see the NS 200 Locomotive series firsthand. Hosted in locations that have played a significant role in railroading history, these events will celebrate the generations of people and defining moments that have shaped Norfolk Southern's story. Event locations and additional details will be announced in the coming weeks.
A new GeneratioNS campaign will bring the railroad's history to life through employee storytelling, historical content, and digital experiences that connect the company's past with its future.
Preserving and sharing 200 years of railroad heritage

Norfolk Southern's history is a reflection of the industry itself. The company's early predecessor railroads helped open new markets, support American industry, and connect communities, growing and evolving alongside the growing nation. Those contributions laid the foundation for the railroad's present-day network and continue to influence its role in the nation's transportation system. In 2012, Norfolk Southern painted selection of commemorative units representing railroads that played significant roles in its history. The 22
are used in freight service across the railroad's 22-state network.
To help preserve and share that history, Norfolk Southern is continuing its work with the
Atlanta History Center
and the
Virginia Museum of History & Culture

to preserve, curate, and share the railroad's heritage. As part of the 200th anniversary, that ongoing collaboration will bring history to life through archival photographs and a historical timeline highlighting key moments from the past two centuries.
"Railroad history is deeply connected to the story of America and preserving that history helps us understand how generations of people, innovation, and industry shaped the country we know today,"
said Sheffield Hale, president and CEO of the Atlanta History Center

. "We've been pleased to work with Norfolk Southern to help research and bring together the milestones that tell its 200-year story, while helping preserve important pieces of its rail history for future generations."

"Railroads played a vital role in Virginia history—a far-reaching story of commerce, transportation, and connectivity. Railroads spurred growth and expansion, and provided broad new access for Virginia communities, industries, and markets, and ultimately to ports and the world,"
said Jamie O. Bosket, President and CEO of the Virginia Museum of History & Culture.

"We're proud to partner with Norfolk Southern to explore and share the stories of the people and innovations that shaped this legacy, and to be keepers of vast Norfolk Southern archives that will tell this important history for generations."

While 2027 is a celebration of how far rail has come, it is also about where Norfolk Southern is headed next, carrying forward a legacy of innovation and service as the company continues building a stronger railroad for the future.

About Norfolk Southern
Since 1827, Norfolk Southern Corporation (

) and its predecessor companies have safely moved the goods and materials that drive the U.S. economy. Today, it operates a 22-state freight transportation network. Committed to furthering sustainability, Norfolk Southern helps its customers avoid approximately 15 million tons of yearly carbon emissions by shipping via rail. Its dedicated team members deliver approximately 7 million carloads annually, from agriculture to consumer goods. Norfolk Southern also has the most extensive intermodal network in the eastern U.S. It serves a majority of the country's population and manufacturing base, with connections to every major container port on the Atlantic coast as well as major ports across the Gulf Coast and Great Lakes. Learn more by visiting www.NorfolkSouthern.com.
